newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court opens hearing on Rao bail plea.
newsitem.headline: Indian court opens hearing on Rao bail plea.

text.p: The Delhi High Court on Thursday opened a hearing into a bail plea by former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a criminal forgery case.

"As the Delhi High Court has given bail to number of persons accused of murder and even of corruption... Mr Rao should also be given bail," Rao's lawyer, R.K. Anand, told the court in opening remarks.
Rao, 75, is the first former or serving prime minister to face criminal charges in India. He resigned as prime minister in May after his Congress party was defeated in general elections.

In September, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) charged Rao with aiding the alleged defamation in 1989 of V.P. Singh, a Congress defector who later became prime minister, with the help of forged papers showing an illegal bank account.
He has been charged in two other criminal cases -- for allegedly cheating a businessman of $100,000 in 1983 and buying votes in a 1993 election. Rao has denied any wrongdoing.
The three charges each carry maximum penalties of between five and seven years in jail.
Rao was denied bail in the forgery case by Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Prem Kumar on Tuesday and given until November 13 to appeal to a higher court.
Court sources said legal arguments in the latest bail plea could be lengthy and a ruling was unlikely on Thursday.
If denied bail, Rao can appeal to the Supreme Court. But if he is rebuffed by the Supreme Court, he would have to surrender to the lower court on or before November 13, legal experts said.
On Wednesday, a Delhi judge granted Rao indefinite bail in the 1983 cheating case.
